text: RWB-S8-E2012-APP starts on Day 1 with Depends on (build) = None, as the split plan states, and builds against the platform contract baselines and fakes the DP table names (DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15, DP-19). The eight platform H rows and two C rows are carried in section 13 as tracked, and none of them blocks the start.
why: Every pattern of the story adds a platform contract row, but the plan carries no H row for this slice, so either the plan is incomplete or the platform rows are not build dependencies. Template and Rules v1 section R5.7 makes a story with only CON H dependencies Day 1, and the coordinator's plan is the authority on H.
read: Template and Rules v1 sections R5.5 and R5.7; _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json slice RWB-S8-E2012-APP
applied_in: Metadata Depends on (build) and Ready to start; section 3; section 13
impact: The build starts on the platform stubs; a later platform change is absorbed by the versions of the libraries, not by this story.

text: The operation names, paths and schemas of the consumed contracts other than RWB-P3-E2012-CON are taken from the CON story of each owner as it is published: the case-record read of rwb-case, the reference-data read of rwb-case, the package read of rwb-decision, the authorise call of rwb-access and the case-facts read of rwb-source-data. Until then they are called through generated clients against WireMock fakes with the same shapes.
why: The legacy story names one transfer endpoint and one case read and no operation for the four other answers this slice needs, and no architecture slide publishes paths for them.
read: RWB-E2-012 section 12; context pack S8 ownership rows; Arch v5 slide 13
confirm: Solution architect when the CON stories are baselined
impact: A renamed operation is a client change only; the behaviour, the 2 s budget and the breaker stay.

text: This service publishes GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations as the open-deviation answer the rwb-case move and the SCR-05 deviation panel read, one hop with a 2 s budget, and keeps DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared as the events that feed recovery_case.deviation_open. The read is treated as the service's third operation although the Ownership Map lists two writes.
why: The P3 slice of the same legacy key names exactly this read as the answer it needs, and rwb-case may not read the deviation table. The Ownership Map gives two write operations only, and the connection matrix also has rwb-case listening to S8 events, so one fact is described twice; the read is the one the refusing move depends on.
read: RWB-P3-E2012-APP sections 12.2 and 13; context pack S8 REST operations provided; Arch v5 slide 13; RWB-E2-012 section 11
confirm: Solution architect and the CON story of this service
impact: The read's exact schema is fixed by the CON story; the panel and the move both build against it, so a change is one contract version.

text: The conditions, actions and target owners of R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 come from the Business Rules and Routing Logic workbook at build time, and the SCR-05 deviation fragment is rendered as a table of code, handler, paused state, contact stop and rule ID, with the refusal message beneath it and the cleared row shown as history.
why: No source gives those four rule rows and no source draws the fragment; the panel must still render something, and the workbook is the named authority for DEV rows in FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 and TSD S8 T4.
read: FSD S8 A2.4.3.1 and A2.9; TSD S8 T4; RWB-E2-012 section 15
confirm: Business lead and the screen owner
impact: A missing row leaves the panel without that code's owner label; no case state depends on it.

text: The case status and legal-hold changes are consumed as an event group of rwb-case whose names are not yet published; the consumer group is declared against the placeholder and faked with the platform inbox stub. CaseTransferred is consumed under its published name rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1.
why: The connection matrix gives S8 an event subscription to rwb-case and publishes no event name; only CaseTransferred is named, in the legacy story, so the other two facts cannot be bound.
read: Arch v5 slide 13; RWB-E2-012 section 4 step 4 and section 14; context pack S8
confirm: Solution architect when the rwb-case event catalogue is published
impact: Only the panel's hold and status reading depends on the group; the move and the refusal do not.

text: No column is added to deviation. The reason code, the rule ID and the package version of a move are held in the local decision record of DP-03, and the queue, team, owner, deviation flag and legal hold are read on the rwb-case contract. The deviation row keeps its code, handler, paused state, contact stop, raised-at, return point, cleared-at and outcome only.
why: deviation holds no transfer field (TSD S8 T3.1), the legacy write set is on rwb_case and assignment, and DP-01 forbids writing another service's tables.
read: TSD S8 T3.1; RWB-E2-012 section 11; context pack S8 table list
confirm: Data owner at the CON and DB stories
impact: A query for the reason or the rule version of a move reads the decision record, not the deviation row.

text: LOV-TRANSFER-REASON carries R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue as the intended set pending DL23, read at its version on the rwb-case reference-data contract and never written in code.
why: The legacy story states those six codes as assumed values marked DL23, and no approved list exists; the screen must still render a reason list, and the reference data is the only place it may come from.
impact: A changed list is a reference-data load, not a code change; the panel label follows automatically.

text: The fifteen legacy test case IDs of RWB-E2-012 are kept in both slices. This file records them at Component and NFR level as the deviation-side proof, and the P3 file records the same ids at End to end and NFR for the move itself; the assembly keeps one master row per legacy ID with both slices named against it.
why: The split plan gives the same tcs_legacy array to both slices, so dropping the ids here would leave the deviation side without proof, and changing them would break the legacy trace.
read: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json tcs_legacy of both slices; RWB-P3-E2012-APP section 16
impact: A test case ID resolves to two story rows; the master shows the level per slice and runs the union.
